thread:
jen li: Quick question 12 I just got a surprise bill for an at-home genetic test. Lab billed CPT 81256 and the carrier portal shows it as out-of-network. I used the lab's prepaid kit but the lab's parent billing address is out-of-state. Is this covered on Plus?

alex r: Hey Jen 12 which Redwood plan did you use (Standard vs Plus)? Also DM last 4 of member ID—don't post PHI here.

jen li: Plus. DM'd the last 4 (1234). The lab says they're contracted with the insurer but the portal flags OON. Very confusing.

marc (benefits): Hi Jen 12 common situation: genetic/diagnostic labs sometimes require a prior auth AND require the performing lab (billing NPI) to be in-network. Some ship-to or specimen-processing labs bill from a different legal entity that isn't contracted, causing OON adjudication.

marc (benefits): We can do three things: 1) verify lab network status for CPT 81256 with the carrier, 2) request/verify prior authorization if needed, 3) if carrier paid as OON, file an appeal arguing the lab is in-network per contract or request reprocessing.

jen li: Sounds good. I have the kit invoice and shipping tracking. Where should I send them?

benefits-team: Please upload medical bills, invoices, and any shipping docs to the secure benefits claims portal: https://benefits.redwood-inc/claims-upload. If docs contain PHI and you prefer, DM a benefits rep or open a secure ticket.

people-ops-bot: Carrier lab support: GenLabCare 1-800-555-1212. Carrier claims lookup: https://carrier-portal.example/claims (have member ID + claim # ready).

marc (benefits): Posting a quick appeal template you can use or send to the lab billing team: ```To: claims@carrier.com
Member: Jen Li (DOB: mm/dd/yyyy)
Member ID: XXXX-XXXX-1234
Claim #: [insert claim number]
Service: Genetic test CPT 81256 performed by [Lab Name]
Issue: Claim adjudicated as out-of-network despite provider/parent lab being listed as in-network per vendor contract. Please reprocess or provide contract reference showing out-of-network status.
Attached: invoice, shipping tracking, lab report, prior auth (if applicable)
Thank you,
[Member / Provider representative]```

alex r: Marc, can you confirm whether Plus requires prior auth for 81256 when billed as diagnostic vs screening? If it does, can ops help request the auth?

marc (benefits): On Plus, CPT 81256 typically requires prior auth when it's diagnostic or medically necessary. I'll open a carrier verification ticket and request expedited auth confirmation. Please share the lab billing NPI and the claim number when you have them.

jen li: Got it. NPI: 9876543210. Claim #: 2025-44321. Uploaded the invoice + tracking to the portal a few mins ago. Thanks! :pray: 

benefits-team: Received. Intake ticket #BP-2025-778 created and assigned to carrier outreach. We'll post updates in this thread.

jen li: Appreciate it. If the appeal fails, what's our reimbursement path? Submit OON reimbursement or appeal first?

marc (benefits): We always appeal first (we're initiating that). If appeal is denied AND lab truly is OON, you can submit for out-of-network reimbursement via the benefits portal. Typical turnaround 7-14 business days after all docs are in. Keep originals and any provider statements.

alex r: If needed we can escalate to our carrier rep (enterprise channel) to speed verification. Marc, can you loop them in if carrier is slow?

marc (benefits): Yep, will escalate if no response in 3 business days. Also if the carrier requests clinical justification we can coordinate with the ordering clinician to provide notes.

jen li: Please escalate if it gets stuck. Thanks everyone for the quick help.

people-ops-bot: Update: Ticket BP-2025-778 assigned to carrier rep. Expected response ETA: 3 business days.

alex r: Thanks Jen 12 we'll monitor and keep you updated here. :slightly_smiling_face:
